title: The Doctrine of God
summary: Who God is: His existence, His attributes, His names, and His sovereign will.
description: Everything in theology depends on who God is. This course studies how we can know God, His greatness (attributes that belong to Him alone, such as eternity and unchangeableness), His goodness (qualities He shares in part with us, such as love and holiness), His names in Scripture, and His sovereign rule over all things. Each truth is shown from the Bible and applied to worship and daily trust.
objectives: Show how God can be known and why His existence is evident
Explain God's attributes simply and biblically
Introduce the main names of God in Scripture
Explain God's sovereignty, will and providence
outcomes: Explain God's eternity, omnipresence, omniscience and omnipotence
Explain God's holiness, love, justice, mercy and faithfulness
Give the meaning of key Hebrew names of God
Show how knowing God shapes worship, trust and obedience

modules.title: Knowing God
modules.intro: Can finite people know the infinite God? This week we see that God is knowable because He has made Himself known.

lessons.title: The God who is there
lessons.body:
The Bible does not argue for God's existence at length; it begins, "In the beginning God" (Genesis 1:1). It says creation plainly shows His power and Godhead, so that people are without excuse (Romans 1:20), and that "The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God" (Psalm 14:1).

Thoughtful people have given reasons: the existence of the universe needs a cause; its order points to a designer; the moral law in our conscience points to a Lawgiver.

Yet true knowledge of God comes by faith in His revelation: "he that cometh to God must believe that he is" (Hebrews 11:6).

lessons.title: Knowable yet beyond us
lessons.body:
God is **incomprehensible**: we can never know Him fully. "Canst thou by searching find out God?" (Job 11:7). "His greatness is unsearchable" (Psalm 145:3).

Yet God is **knowable**: we can know Him truly, because He has spoken. Jesus said, "this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God" (John 17:3).

Both truths matter. The first keeps us humble and full of wonder; the second gives us confidence and joy. We will spend eternity learning more of Him.

lessons.title: Knowing about God and knowing God
lessons.body:
It is possible to know many facts about God without knowing Him personally. The demons believe there is one God, and tremble (James 2:19).

God says, "let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me" (Jeremiah 9:24). Paul's great desire was "That I may know him" (Philippians 3:10).

Knowing God means a relationship: trusting Him, loving Him, obeying Him and enjoying His presence. Doctrine is the map; fellowship with God is the journey.

terms.def: Beyond full understanding; God can never be known completely.
Able to be truly known, because God has revealed Himself.
Belief in one personal God who created and rules the world.
The denial that God exists.
The reasoning that the universe's existence requires a first cause.
The reasoning that the moral law within us points to a divine Lawgiver.

texts.teaches: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Whoever comes to God must believe that He is.
God's greatness is unsearchable.
Eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ.
Glory only in understanding and knowing the LORD.

summary: Scripture assumes God's existence; creation and conscience testify to it.
God is beyond full understanding, yet truly knowable through revelation.
Knowing God is more than knowing facts about Him.
Eternal life is a personal knowledge of God through Christ.

modules.title: The Greatness of God
modules.intro: Some attributes belong to God alone. This week we study His self-existence, eternity, unchangeableness, presence, knowledge and power.

lessons.title: Self-existent, eternal, unchanging
lessons.body:
God is **self-existent**: He depends on nothing. "I AM THAT I AM" (Exodus 3:14). He has life in Himself (John 5:26).

God is **eternal**: without beginning or end. "From everlasting to everlasting, thou art God" (Psalm 90:2).

God is **immutable** (unchanging) in His being, character and promises: "I am the LORD, I change not" (Malachi 3:6). Where Scripture says God "repented", it describes Him responding as He promised to people's change, without any change in His nature or purpose (Jonah 3:10; Numbers 23:19).

lessons.title: Everywhere present, all-knowing
lessons.body:
God is **omnipresent**: present everywhere with His whole being. "Whither shall I flee from thy presence?" (Psalm 139:7). He is not spread out like air; He is fully present in every place.

God is **omniscient**: He knows all things, past, present, future and possible. "Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight" (Hebrews 4:13). He knows our thoughts before we speak (Psalm 139:4).

These truths warn us that nothing is hidden, and comfort us that God sees every tear and need.

lessons.title: All-powerful
lessons.body:
God is **omnipotent**: He can do all that He wills. "Is any thing too hard for the LORD?" (Genesis 18:14). "With God all things are possible" (Matthew 19:26).

Omnipotence does not mean God can do what contradicts His nature. He "cannot lie" (Titus 1:2) or deny Himself (2 Timothy 2:13). This is not weakness but perfection.

God's power created the world, raised Christ from the dead (Ephesians 1:19-20), and keeps His people. Jeremiah prayed, "there is nothing too hard for thee" (Jeremiah 32:17).

terms.def: Qualities that belong to God alone, such as eternity and omnipresence.
God depends on nothing outside Himself for His existence.
God has no beginning or end.
God does not change in His being, character or purposes.
God is fully present everywhere.
God knows all things perfectly.
God is able to do all that He wills.

texts.teaches: God's name I AM THAT I AM shows He is self-existent.
From everlasting to everlasting, God is God.
The LORD does not change.
There is nowhere to flee from God's presence.
Nothing is too hard for the Lord GOD.

summary: God is self-existent, eternal and unchanging.
He is present everywhere and knows all things.
He is all-powerful, yet never acts against His own nature.
These truths humble us and give great comfort.

modules.title: The Goodness of God
modules.intro: Some of God's qualities are reflected, in part, in His people. This week: holiness, love, justice, mercy, grace and faithfulness.

lessons.title: Holy, holy, holy
lessons.body:
Holiness is God's majestic separateness from all creation and His perfect moral purity. The seraphim cry, "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts" (Isaiah 6:3). Holiness is the only attribute repeated three times like this.

God's holiness exposed Isaiah's sin ("Woe is me!") and then provided cleansing (Isaiah 6:5-7).

God calls His people to share His holiness: "Be ye holy; for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16). This is a **communicable** attribute: we reflect it, imperfectly now, perfectly in glory.

lessons.title: Love, grace and mercy
lessons.body:
"God is love" (1 John 4:8). He loves freely, not because we are lovely. "God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us" (Romans 5:8).

Two words describe God's love toward sinners:
- **Grace** is God's undeserved favour, giving us what we do not deserve (Ephesians 2:8).
- **Mercy** is God's compassion, withholding the punishment we do deserve (Titus 3:5).

God is also **good** and **patient**: "The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy" (Psalm 103:8).

lessons.title: Just and faithful
lessons.body:
God is **righteous and just**: He always does what is right and will punish sin. "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" (Genesis 18:25). His justice is not cancelled by His love; at the cross both meet, so that God is "just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus" (Romans 3:26).

God is **faithful**: He keeps every promise. "Great is thy faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23). "If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful" (2 Timothy 2:13).

We can rest our whole weight on God's character.

modules.title: The Names of God
modules.intro: In Scripture a name reveals character. This week we study the main names by which God makes Himself known.

lessons.title: Elohim, Adonai and Jehovah
lessons.body:
**Elohim** is the general Hebrew word for God, used in Genesis 1:1. It is plural in form though used with singular verbs, which many see as a hint of the fulness of the Godhead.

**Adonai** means Lord or Master, expressing God's authority and our service.

**Jehovah** (or Yahweh), written in the KJV as LORD in capital letters, is God's personal covenant name, revealed to Moses: "I AM THAT I AM" (Exodus 3:14-15; 6:3). It speaks of God's self-existence and faithfulness to His covenant people.

lessons.title: Compound names of the LORD
lessons.body:
Scripture joins God's covenant name to descriptions of what He does:

- **Jehovah-jireh:** the LORD will provide (Genesis 22:14).
- **Jehovah-rapha:** the LORD that healeth thee (Exodus 15:26).
- **Jehovah-nissi:** the LORD my banner (Exodus 17:15).
- **Jehovah-shalom:** the LORD send peace (Judges 6:24).
- **Jehovah-tsidkenu:** THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS (Jeremiah 23:6).
- **Jehovah-shammah:** the LORD is there (Ezekiel 48:35).

Each arose from a real situation and became a lasting promise.

lessons.title: God most high, Almighty, Father
lessons.body:
**El Elyon**, God most high, possessor of heaven and earth (Genesis 14:19). **El Shaddai**, God Almighty, the all-sufficient one who made promises to Abraham (Genesis 17:1). **The LORD of hosts** (Jehovah Sabaoth), commander of heaven's armies (1 Samuel 1:3).

In the New Testament, Jesus taught us to call God **Father** (Matthew 6:9). Through the Spirit of adoption, believers cry "Abba, Father" (Romans 8:15).

Knowing God's names helps us pray: we call on Him according to who He has revealed Himself to be.

modules.title: The Sovereign God
modules.intro: God rules over all things. This week we study His sovereignty, His will and His providence, and what they mean for our trust.

lessons.title: God reigns
lessons.body:
God's sovereignty is His supreme rule and authority over all things. "Our God is in the heavens: he hath done whatsoever he hath pleased" (Psalm 115:3). Even Nebuchadnezzar confessed that God "doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth" (Daniel 4:35).

God "worketh all things after the counsel of his own will" (Ephesians 1:11). Nothing takes Him by surprise; no plan of His fails (Isaiah 46:10).

This does not make people robots. Scripture holds both truths: God reigns, and people make real choices for which they are responsible (Acts 2:23).

lessons.title: God's will
lessons.body:
Theologians speak of God's will in two senses:

- His **decreed** (secret) will: what God has purposed to happen, which always comes to pass (Ephesians 1:11).
- His **revealed** (moral) will: what God commands us to do, which we can obey or disobey (1 Thessalonians 4:3).

"The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us" (Deuteronomy 29:29).

For guidance, we focus on God's revealed will in Scripture, and trust Him with what is hidden.

lessons.title: Providence and trust
lessons.body:
**Providence** is God's continuing care and control of all He has made. He upholds all things by His word (Hebrews 1:3), feeds the birds and clothes the lilies (Matthew 6:26-30), and not a sparrow falls without Him (Matthew 10:29).

He works even through evil for good: Joseph's brothers meant evil, "but God meant it unto good" (Genesis 50:20). "All things work together for good to them that love God" (Romans 8:28).

Sovereignty is a pillow for the believer: we can be at peace, pray with confidence and serve without fear, because our Father reigns.

terms.def: God's supreme rule and authority over all things.
God's eternal purpose for all that happens, which always comes to pass.
God's commands in Scripture, which we are to obey.
God's ongoing care and control of all creation.
People's real accountability for their choices, alongside God's rule.

summary: God reigns over all things and His purposes never fail.
God's sovereignty and human responsibility are both taught in Scripture.
We obey God's revealed will and trust Him with His secret will.

short.q: Explain the difference between God being incomprehensible and knowable.
short.model: God can never be fully understood (incomprehensible), yet He can be truly known because He has revealed Himself (knowable).

short.q: Define God's omniscience and give one comfort it brings.
short.model: God knows all things perfectly; this comforts believers because He sees every need and tear.

short.q: What is the difference between grace and mercy?
short.model: Grace is God's undeserved favour, giving what we do not deserve; mercy withholds the punishment we do deserve.

short.q: How do God's love and justice meet at the cross?
short.model: At the cross God punished sin in Christ, satisfying His justice, and in love provided salvation, so He is just and the justifier of believers.

short.q: What do the names Jehovah-jireh and Jehovah-rapha mean?
short.model: Jehovah-jireh means 'the LORD will provide'; Jehovah-rapha means 'the LORD that healeth thee'.

short.q: Explain God's providence with one Bible example.
short.model: Providence is God's ongoing care and control of all things, as when He turned Joseph's brothers' evil into good.

assignments.title: An attribute in my life
assignments.prompt: Choose one attribute of God from this course. Explain it from at least three passages, then describe how believing it should change your prayer, your fears and your obedience this week.

assignments.title: Praying God's names
assignments.prompt: Write a prayer, and a short explanation, using at least four names of God from Week 4. For each name, give its meaning and reference and explain why you are calling on God by that name.
